PHYSICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #11
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: PHYSICS
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Milk souring

2. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Producers
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Decomposers only

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Photoelectric effect? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Photoelectric effect.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Photoelectric effect.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Photoelectric effect.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Photoelectric effect.

4. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Thin lenses? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Thin lenses.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Thin lenses.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Thin lenses.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Thin lenses.

6. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only carbon dioxide

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Circular motion? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Circular motion.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Circular motion.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Circular motion.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Circular motion.

8. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

9. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

10. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. newton (N)
   C. joule (J)
   D. watt (W)

11. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Transistors? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Transistors.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Transistors.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Transistors.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Transistors.

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Satellites? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Satellites.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Satellites.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Satellites.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Satellites.

14. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS.

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Dynamics? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Dynamics.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Dynamics.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Dynamics.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Dynamics.

17. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electromagnetic induction? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electromagnetic induction.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electromagnetic induction.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electromagnetic induction.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Electromagnetic induction.

18. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Floating and Sinking? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Floating and Sinking.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Floating and Sinking.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Floating and Sinking.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Floating and Sinking.

19. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 0 °C

20. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Mains electricity? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Mains electricity.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mains electricity.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Mains electricity.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Mains electricity.

21. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Quantity of Heat? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Quantity of Heat.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Quantity of Heat.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Quantity of Heat.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Quantity of Heat.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
22. In three clear sentences, explain Floating and Sinking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Quantity of Heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Thin lenses and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Photoelectric effect and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

26. In three clear sentences, explain Electromagnetic induction and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

27. In three clear sentences, explain Mains electricity and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

28. In three clear sentences, explain Transistors and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

29. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

30. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Satellites and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

31. In three clear sentences, explain Dynamics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
